SELECTED_INDEX: 8
CONFIDENCE: 0.55
EXPLANATION: The very strong Raman line at 1333 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of the symmetric ν(NO₂) stretch (rule GFQ-022); among the ten candidates only molecule 8 (O=[N+]([O-])c1ccncc1F) contains a nitro group.  A weaker band at 1555 cm⁻¹ matches the ν_as(NO₂) region, and the 852 cm⁻¹ peak fits the NO₂ out-of-plane deformation.  Peaks at 1607, 1222, 1192 and 1006 cm⁻¹ as well as the C–H stretches at 3073/3115 cm⁻¹ are all typical of an aromatic (pyridine) ring bearing a fluorine substituent; C–F stretching/bending modes often appear near 1000–1150 cm⁻¹, consistent with the 1006 and 1134 cm⁻¹ bands.  No other candidate simultaneously offers NO₂ and C–F functionalities to account for these key features.  Therefore candidate 8 best explains the observed spectrum.
